title: Analysis of lysosomal hydrolase trafficking and activity in human iPSC-derived neuronal models
protocol: Use a cell scraper to scrape cell cultures from a 12 or 6-well dish into 1 mL cold 1× PBS.
Centrifuge the scraped cells at 400 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend pelleted material in an appropriate volume of cold protein extraction buffer containing 1% Triton X-100.
Homogenize the extract using a Teflon homogenizer with a motor-driven spindle 20–40 times at 2,000 × g.
Incubate the extract in an ice-water slurry with gentle rotation for 20 minutes.
Use care not to generate excessive froth when homogenizing the cell pellets.
Homogenize the extract until it is even and slightly translucent; add more lysis buffer if necessary.
Centrifuge the clarified extract at 20,000 × g, 4°C for 10 min.
Transfer the supernatants to a new 1.5 mL tube.
Perform a protein assay on the supernatant using a Pierce micro BCA kit or standard Bradford reagent.
Digest the lysate with Endoglycosidase H (Endo H) and PNGase F in two separate tubes after denaturing the sample.
Denature 50 μg of protein lysate by adding up to 18 μL water, then add 2 μL of 10× denaturation buffer and incubate at 100°C for 10 min.
Pulse-centrifuge the sample after denaturing to spin down any evaporated liquid.
Add 2.5 μL of 10× G5 digest buffer, 1.5 μL of water, and 1 μL of Endo H to the tube and incubate for 2 h at 37°C.
Add 2.6 μL of 10× G5 buffer to the sample.
Pipette 2.6 μL of 10% NP-40 into the sample.
Incubate the sample with 1 μL of PNGase F for 2 h at 37°C.
Prepare an undigested control sample by using water instead of enzymes and incubating under the same conditions as experimental samples.
Boil digest samples in 1× Laemmli sample buffer for 10 min at 100°C.
Run the samples on 10% Tris-glycine gels that are 1.5 mm thick, using an initial voltage of 120 V for 20 min followed by 150 V until a 36 kDa marker is 1 cm from the bottom of the gel.
Stop gels at appropriate times to prevent run-off of protein forms migrating between 10–20 kDa.
Transfer onto PVDF membranes according to the transfer apparatus used.
Transfer for 1 hour at 20°C at a constant voltage of 20–30 V (approximately 300 mA starting current per gel).
Remove the membrane and postfix in 100% MeOH for 1 minute.
Wash the membrane in 1× Tris-buffered saline (pH 7.4) for 2–5 minutes until the membrane sinks.
Stain the gel in Coomassie brilliant blue for 12–24 hours.
Wash the stained gel in water for 2 hours.
Alternatively, postfix the membrane in 0.4% PFA made in 1× PBS and incubated for 20 minutes on a slow rotator.
Wash the membrane with 3 × 5-minute washes in water after PFA postfixing.
Mix the membrane in a 1:1 ratio of Odyssey Block Buffer (OBB) and 1× TBS (No Tween) for 1–1.5 hours.
Add primary antibodies to a 1:1 mix of OBB and 1× TBS-Tween 0.2%.
Incubate the membrane with the primary antibody solution at 4°C for 12–24 hours.
Wash the membranes three times, each time for 10 minutes in 1× TBS-Tween 0.2% at 20°C.
Add secondary antibodies diluted to a ratio of 1:10,000 in OBB : 1× TBS-Tween 0.2% 1:1 mix and incubate the membranes at 20°C for 1–2 hours.
Wash the membranes three times, each time for 10 minutes in 1× TBS-Tween 0.2% at 20°C.
Scan the western blots using an Odyssey infrared imaging system (or similar).
Analyze the scanned images with imaging software such as Image Studio Software (Li-Cor) or Image J.
By comparing the undigested, Endo H digested, and PNGase F digested samples, identify and quantify the post-ER/ER forms of each protein.
Quantify protein maturation by calculating a ratio of post-ER/ER forms.
Each form can also be quantified separately and normalized to a loading control (e.g., GAPDH, tubulin, or Coomassie blue).
Ensure efficient homogenization during the lysis step using a fresh enzyme for complete digestion of samples.
Avoid gradient gels; use acrylamide percentage suited for the protein of interest (10% polyacrylamide for most proteins averaging 50–70 kDa in weight).
Use an antibody capable of detecting mature and immature forms to achieve accurate detection.
Plate cells on PDL and laminin-coated coverglass in 24 or 12 well plastic culture plates.
Quickly remove the culture media from the plates.
Immediately add 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 1× PBS for 20 min at 20°C under a fume hood.
Remove the 4% PFA and wash the cells 3 times for 5 min in cold PBS to completely remove PFA.
Permeabilize and block cells with 0.2% saponin (w/v)/1× PBS for 5 min.
Block the cells with 0.2% (w/v) glycine/0.2% saponin in 1× PBS for additional minutes after initial permeabilization.
Prepare a blocking solution of 2% bovine serum albumin, 5% normal goat serum in 0.2% saponin/1× PBS.
Incubate cells with the blocking solution for 30 min.
Dilute anti-GCase primary antibody to a 1:1,000 dilution in the blocking buffer.
Place a 50 μL droplet of diluted primary antibody onto parafilm inside a humidity chamber.
Carefully remove cover glasses from plastic culture plate and flip onto the primary antibody solution so that the cell-side is facing down.
Incubate cover glasses with primary antibodies for 12–24 h at 4°C.
Wash cells very gently 3 times for 20 min each in 0.1% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS at 20°C the next day.
Avoid using a vacuum aspirator during wash steps for iPSC-derived neurons.
Use gentle pipetting with a P-1000 tip for wash steps.
Spin down secondary antibody stocks for 10 min, 20,000 × g, 4°C before use to avoid aggregates.
Add secondary antibodies at 1:300 or 1:400 dilutions in blocking buffer for 2 hours at 20°C.
Wash cells three times for 20 minutes each with 0.1% Triton in 1× PBS at 20°C.
Place a 5-10 μL droplet of DAPI-containing Fluoromount G on a glass slide.
Rinse cover glasses quickly in pure water, then invert onto slides containing Fluoromount G.
Remove any bubbles and allow to dry for 10 minutes.
Seal edges with a thin layer of clear nail polish.
Dry the slides at 20°C for 24 hours in the dark.
Store slides long-term at 4°C.
Image cells within one week by confocal microscopy through a 1 μm section by Z-stack at 1 μm per section.
Using Image J software, outline individual cells and define them as regions of interest to be calculated individually.
Obtain Pearson's correlation values for colocalization using ImageJ software using the Coloc 2 plugin.
Add an artificial substrate into the media of living cell cultures for hydrolase activity measurement.
Allow cells to internalize and traffic the substrate to lysosomes through the endolysosomal system within 30 min.
Monitor fluorescein signal over time as it accumulates within lysosomal compartments.
Treat parallel cultures with a lysosomal inhibitor such as Bafilomycin A1 (Baf A1) to reduce lysosomal acidity.
Estimate specific lysosomal activity by comparing control and Baf A1 treated cultures.
Add dextran cascade blue to cells at a final concentration of 1 mg/mL 12–24 hours before starting activity measurements.
Do not treat one or two wells; these will serve as blank controls.
Measure lysosomal activity (5 h).
For half of the wells, add Baf A1 to achieve a final concentration of 200 nM by adding 11 μL of 2 μM Baf A1 to each well containing 100 μL media.
Add an equal volume of DMSO to control wells.
Incubate cells with Baf A1 and dextran blue for 1 hour at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Aspirate off the media after incubation to remove dextran blue.
Replace media with fresh media containing the fluorescent substrate of the lysosomal enzyme being analyzed.
For GCase analysis, use PFB-FD-Gluc at 100 μg/mL for 30–45 minutes.
Ensure that Baf A1 or DMSO is present in appropriate wells during incubation.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 45 min.
Gently wash the cells once with complete media.
Replace the media in appropriate wells with complete media containing either DMSO or Baf A1.
Ensure the volume of media in each well is precise.
For iPSC-neurons, use complete Neural basal (NB) media supplemented with B27.
Replace the media with 100 μL/well of SM1-NB media without PFB-FD-Gluc and phenol red.
Avoid letting the cells dry out or lift off during media changes.
Immediately read the plate in the microplate reader to get the initial fluorescent reading.
Set the temperature of the plate reader to 37°C.
Ensure the plate reader is configured for bottom reading fluorescence.
Adjust sensitivity settings if necessary (6 PMT at medium).
Use well-scan setting in Softmax software if cells are clumped together.
Wait for a minimal signal at time = 0 since substrate requires approximately 30 min post-chasing time to accumulate inside lysosomes.
Expect a strong dextran blue signal at t = 0 that should remain consistent between initial and final readings.
Cover the plate with foil after the first reading to protect from light.
Place the plate back into the incubator after covering it with foil.
Read the plate every 30 min for up to 4 h to obtain a full kinetic activity curve.
Return the plate to the humidified tissue culture incubator after each read.
Do not perform further media changes during the experiment.
Remove the media after the final read.
Fix the cells in 4% PFA for 20 minutes.
Stain the cells with a primary antibody for neurofilament if activity is measured in neurons.
Incubate the stained cells with a secondary antibody IRDye800.
Observe and document neurite degeneration based on the decline in neurofilament staining.
Use CellTag700 for total cell volume staining or Draq5 for specific nuclear staining.
Incubate stained cells at 20°C for 1 hour.
Wash the stained cells with 1× PBS.
Scan the plates on an infrared imager such as Li-cor Odyssey, Azure Sapphire, or Typhoon system.
Normalize the lysosomal substrate signal to total cellular material per well indicated by CellTag700 and Draq5.
Normalize relative fluorescent units (RFUs) of hydrolase substrate for each time point to cell volume or lysosomal mass.
Plot normalized RFUs versus time.
If normalizing to lysosomal mass, normalize values to the last time point collected of dextran cascade blue.
Prepare experiments to compare the effect of small molecules that activate lysosomes.
Use 8-10 wells per experiment (4-5 each for DMSO and Baf A1).
Include 2 or 3 distinct cell passages/differentiations per analysis.
Conduct analyses in a blinded manner if possible.
